Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

record noun

a written account kept for later

also records, register, keep a record, public records, minutes

classical

Cic. Arch. 8: tabulae pūblicae (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fl. 40

1A gramophone record (“a vinyl record”) is orbis phōnographicus in Traupman 53; that sense has no record here.

tabulae1, tabulārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural

records, registers, accounts

Properly writing tablets, then anything written on them: accounts, lists, registers and the public records (tabulae pūblicae). See document.

Other words

  • commentārius, commentāriī m. — notebook, memorandum, journal

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Suet. Aug. 64: commentāriī diurnī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 7.3.7: in commentārium (Lewis & Short, s.v. referō)

    A private record: notes kept for oneself, a day-book; in the plural also memoirs (Caesar’s Commentāriī).

  • 2ācta: long a (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). The neuter plural of āctus, from agō: Gell. 9.6.3 reports āctitō with a long vowel, as from āctus. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

    ācta2, āctōrum n. pl. — records of proceedings

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. agō

    The record of what was done, especially the official gazette (ācta diurna) and minutes.

Examples

  • quī dē tabulīs pūblicīs recitat

    the man who reads from the public recordsCic. Fl. 40 (Lewis & Short)

See also document, list, record, register.

SourcesLewis & Short: tabula · Lewis & Short: commentarius · Lewis & Short: ago
